findings.title: EOF turns a valid frame prefix into different operation content
findings.summary: The kvstore integration encodes peer messages as newline-delimited text, and the receiver dispatches lines accepted by the decoder. Scenario 1 hypothesizes that if a connection ends cleanly after transmitting a valid nonempty prefix of a frame, the receiver can accept the unterminated final token as different operation content instead of rejecting an incomplete frame. The modeling brief reports process-level evidence where a large value was shortened and later returned to a fresh client after both survivors committed the shortened value. This candidate is not covered by an MC finding in the structured source, so it is emitted for confirmation with invariant, config, and counterexample unset.

findings.title: Quorum-selected history across view changes and rolling recovery
findings.summary: The library can install a new view using a DoViewChange quorum that need not include the new primary's own state. Scenario 2 asks whether quorum history selection, volatile recovery resets, log installation, and commit advancement always preserve already committed or client-completed operations in their original positions across rolling recoveries. The mechanism is contract-sensitive because uncommitted suffixes may legitimately be replaced, while committed prefixes and observed client results must remain recoverable. This candidate is not covered by an MC finding in the structured source, so it is emitted for confirmation with invariant, config, and counterexample unset.

findings.title: Arrival-order recovery responses during changing views
findings.summary: Recovery stores responses in a per-sender map, so later arrival order can replace a previously stored response from the same sender and fresh nonce. Scenario 3 asks whether authentic recovery responses generated at different times or views can pass the persisted-view floor and latest-primary-state guards while causing committed-history harm or client-visible inconsistency after further recovery or view-change steps. The mechanism is specifically about same-attempt response overwrite and mixed-view timing, not stale nonce reuse. This candidate is not covered by an MC finding in the structured source, so it is emitted for confirmation with invariant, config, and counterexample unset.

findings.title: Durable view with only some output published before a crash
findings.summary: The caller is required to persist the view before releasing outputs, but a single local step can still produce multiple messages or replies that are published individually. Scenario 4 asks whether a crash after persisting the view and releasing only a prefix of the output sequence can leave authentic in-flight messages while unpublished output and volatile state disappear. The candidate composes this publication boundary with DoViewChange, StartView, recovery, and commit replies to check for committed-history or client-linearizability harm. This candidate is not covered by an MC finding in the structured source, so it is emitted for confirmation with invariant, config, and counterexample unset.

findings.title: Continued requests with a permanently unavailable minority
findings.summary: The implementation uses round-robin primary selection, acknowledgements, state transfer, recovery, retry timers, and capped backoff to make progress. Scenario 5 asks whether, after a finite fault prefix leaves a healthy participating majority and one permanently unavailable minority replica, continuing client requests always complete under explicit delivery and timer fairness. The scenario excludes the previously known shared-sender obstruction and distinguishes finite delay from real non-progress after the stability conditions hold. This candidate is not covered by an MC finding in the structured source, so it is emitted for confirmation with invariant, config, and counterexample unset.
